frontMatter.welcome:
We’re thrilled to have you as part of the family! As a new member, you join us on our journey of heritage, innovation, and sustainability. We believe each employee contributes directly to our growth, and we’re excited for the fresh perspectives you’ll bring.
Our company values – Commitment, Integrity, and Excellence – shape every action we take. They drive us to deliver high-quality products, to support our clients’ diverse needs. bearing in mind the four pillars of sustainability. We encourage you to embody these values as they’ll guide your journey with us and foster personal and professional success.
Your first few weeks may be a whirlwind of training and new information, so take it step by step. This handbook was created to outline expectations, company policies, and the programs available to support you. We’re here to make sure your experience is enriching, enjoyable, and meaningful. Welcome aboard!
With a proud legacy, we combine our traditional values with innovative techniques to produce environmentally responsible products
We are dedicated to producing our products as per the requirement of our customers to the best of quality keeping in mind the current environmental issues. We are dedicated to walking the path of sustainability with the same dedication as much as we are dedicated to quality.
Our commitment to excellence and sustainability drives us to continuously improve and innovate. we focus on:
- Expanding Our Capabilities: By enhancing our competencies, we are able to better serve our customers and build strong partnerships across industries.
- Sustainability and Value Creation: We ensure that not only do we meet industry demands but also contribute to a greener planet by investing in processes that ensure that we do not harm the environment in any way .

chapters.title: Probation and Confirmation
chapters.text:
## Understanding the probation period:
- New employees are placed on a 6-month probation period during which their performance is monitored and evaluated regularly. Feedback is provided to ensure the employee’s success and improvement if needed.
- Post-Probation Confirmation: If the employee successfully meets performance expectations, & good attendance percentage he/she will become confirmed employee.
## Internal Recruitment & Job Shadowing
- At Company , we encourage internal mobility, meaning employees are always welcome to explore different roles within the organization. Job vacancies are communicated internally through email & “Keka Portal”, and team meetings, giving all employees the opportunity to apply for new positions.
- Internal Candidates: Internal employees are given priority in applying for new roles, providing them with growth opportunities to advance or change career paths within the company. This encourages employee retention and promotes career development as prciscibed under “SOP on Job Shadowing & Internal Promotions” ( SOP-HR-05) .
- Support during Internal Transfers: Employees who apply for internal job changes undergo the same interview process as external candidates, ensuring fairness and equal opportunity. HR and the hiring team provide guidance and ensure the process is smooth for all applicants.
## Policy on Original Documents
- Company ensures that we do not retain any original documents from candidates or employees during the recruitment process, providing transparency and ensuring that candidates feel their privacy is respected and upheld throughout their employment journey.
## Record Keeping and Compliance
- All recruitment-related records are securely stored and maintained according to the company’s internal policies, ensuring confidentiality and compliance with privacy standards.
- Recruitment records are periodically reviewed and audited to ensure the process remains fair, transparent, and compliant with regulatory standards, ensuring that hiring practices uphold the highest levels of integrity and professionalism.
## General Administarive matters
- Bus Transport:- In addition to standard administrative services, we also provide bus transport for employees to facilitate easy and convenient commuting to and from the office.
- Canteen Facility: We Provides Lunch, Dinner, & Mid-night Snacks facility to all employees at their designated time as per shift.
## Compensation and Annual Revision Policy
The compensation and benefits framework is vital for Company , directly impacting our ability to attract and retain top talent in both the short and long term. As a growing company in India, achieving success requires us to maintain a competitive edge over our competitors, which means developing a strong position in the marketplace. Employees are essential to this competitive advantage, and effective talent management is crucial in ensuring we remain ahead in the global market. Since compensation plays a central role in attracting and retaining skilled professionals, managing it effectively is key to securing the best talent for our organization.
Company ensures that all employees receive wages that meet or exceed the legally mandated minimum wage standards, as set by government regulations. Additionally, we are committed to ensuring gender pay equality, guaranteeing that employees are paid fairly and equitably, regardless of gender.
To maintain competitiveness, the company will review pay and benefits periodically. This process will take into account various factors, including the business environment, financial situation, ability to pay, sales forecasts, market trends, individual performance, experience, length of service. Our goal is to balance offering competitive pay for key positions with maintaining efficiency, sustainability, and competitiveness in overall manpower costs. Employee compensation will be determined based on the following criteria:
- Importance and criticality of the position
- Responsibilities and deliverables of the role
- Relevant prior experience
- Individual performance and competencies
- Qualifications and educational background
- Availability of talent in the market
At Company , we are committed to ensuring that our compensation revisions are fair, transparent, and based on merit. The following parameters will not be considered when determining salary revisions:
- Gender
- Ethnicity
- Religion
- Domicile
- Caste
- Political affiliation
## Annual Compensation Revision
- Frequency of Revision: Salary revisions are conducted annually for all employees. The revision typically takes effect on April 1st of each year, based on performance during the preceding financial year (April-March).
- Eligibility: Employees who join on or before September 30th will be eligible for the revision in the ongoing financial year.

chapters.title: Wage Equality
chapters.text:
- Company is committed to providing equal pay for equal work, ensuring all employees are compensated fairly for the work they perform, regardless of gender, race, or other personal characteristics.
- A comprehensive wage gap report will be generated annually to provide transparency, highlight any disparities, and track progress toward achieving wage equality across all levels of the company.
- The company follows a structured approach to evaluate roles and responsibilities, ensuring that employees performing the same job or work of equal value receive equal pay. Disparities in pay will be addressed through regular salary audits and adjustments as necessary.
- All pay decisions, including promotions, raises, and, will be based on objective criteria such as skills, experience, performance, and job requirements, rather than personal characteristics or biases.
- India does not declared living wage. The company aspires to match the living wage as and when available for the country.
- Company is committed to regularly reviewing compensation practices to ensure that wage equality is consistently maintained and that any discrepancies are corrected.
- Employees are encouraged to bring forward any concerns about wage inequality to the HR Department, where they will be handled with confidentiality and prompt attention.
- Any identified wage disparities that are found to be discriminatory or unfair will be corrected, and necessary steps will be taken to ensure compliance with legal requirements and organizational standards on wage equality.
- Offer Letter Salary: The salary mentioned in your offer letter is the starting point for your compensation. This amount is clearly defined based on your position, qualifications, experience, and industry standards.
- Online Company Portal: Employees can view their current salary, benefits, and other compensation details through the company's online portal “Keka”. This portal provides real-time access to your salary breakdown, including base pay, allowances, bonuses, and other compensations.
- Salary Bands: Salaries are organized into defined bands based on role and experience. These bands ensure that salaries are competitive and fair within the industry and are aligned with your job level.
## Performance-Based Increments
- Annual Performance Reviews: Salary increments are linked to annual performance reviews, where your achievements, contributions, and growth are assessed. A percentage increase in salary is determined based on these evaluations.
- Review and Update Process: Performance reviews and salary adjustments are communicated transparently via the online portal and through one-on-one meetings with Director HR ( If Required ).
## Leave and Time-Off
- Leave Balances: Your leave balance (annual leave, sick leave, etc.) is tracked and updated regularly in the “Keka” portal. You can view your leave status and apply for leave directly through the portal.
- Leave Approval: All leave requests must be submitted via the portal. Once approved by your Reporting Manager, the leave will be reflected in your payroll calculations.
## Payroll Process
- Salary Payments: Salaries are processed monthly and are transferred directly to the bank account you’ve provided. Payment is made on the 07th of every month. Detailed payslips will be available through the online portal or can collect from HR department for your reference.
- Payslip Details: Your payslip includes your base salary, any bonuses, overtime, allowances, and deductions such as taxes, insurance premiums. It is updated monthly and available for download through the company portal.
Transparent Deductions: Deductions for taxes and other statutory contributions will be clearly listed on your payslip. You can review these deductions and any changes to them at any time via the portal.
## Clear and Open Communication
- Access to Remuneration Details: Employees have full access to their salary and remuneration details, including salary, bonuses, and through the “Keka” online portal.
- Questions and Queries: If you have any questions about your salary, benefits, or remuneration process, you can contact HR directly or review your salary breakdown in the portal for clarity. HR is always available to provide assistance and ensure transparency.

chapters.title: Overtime
chapters.text:
- Overtime work is any time worked beyond the standard working hours of 08.30 a day in any shift.
- Overtime is compensated as per statutory requirement. Employees should seek prior authorization from their supervisor before working overtime.
- The ESSL system will reflect overtime hours and wages in the employee's payroll, ensuring that compensation aligns with Company 's compensation policies and legal requirements.
- In case of any discrepancies or issues with overtime calculations or wages, employees must promptly report them to the HR Department for resolution.
- Any overtime worked beyond the regular schedule must be justified and approved by the respective department head. Employees should ensure they complete overtime hours only when necessary, and in alignment with operational needs.
- Terms and Conditions:
- All overtime worked must be initiated by the Head of Department and approved by HR Department. This request shall be in writing. Only in exceptional circumstances (e.g., a meeting with a client that runs late, a pressing deadline, Audit etc.) can this request be made at the last minute. The Head of department will evaluate last minute requests on a case-by-case basis. An employee who works overtime without prior approval may be subject to corrective action.
- Whenever feasible, efforts should be made to avoid accruing compensatory time by adjusting the employees' work hours within the same work week.
- Refer the “Policy on Wages for detailed A-HR-10
## Career Development and Promotion
At Company , we believe in nurturing employees’ careers based on their performance, potential, and merit.
- Promotion Eligibility: Employees may be promoted to the next level based on an evaluation of their performance and work conduct throughout the year. This evaluation will consider the following criteria:
- Ratings and feedback from the immediate supervisor over the past year.
- Overall behavior and attendance percentage displayed in the workplace.
- Adherence to safety norms and standards throughout the year.
- Reviews and comments received from supervisors or Heads of Departments (HODs).
- Availability of higher-level roles within the organization.
- Merit-Based Promotion: Career growth and promotion will be based solely on merit, with unbiased assessments ensuring equal opportunity for all employees. No discrimination will be tolerated in the promotion process, and all decisions will be made with fairness and transparency.
- Promotion Timing: Promotion cases will be evaluated during the annual salary revision cycle. However, the final decision on promotions and salary revisions rests with the Director HR and Management.
## Promoting Career Mobility
At Company, we believe in empowering our employees through internal career mobility, offering them opportunities to grow and develop across different roles within the organization. Our approach is designed to support professional advancement, foster continuous learning, and align individual goals with the company’s objectives.
## Promotion to New Roles
- Employees who demonstrate the ability, potential, and outstanding performance to excel in new roles are given the support needed for a smooth transition. We offer relevant training and guidance, ensuring that employees are fully prepared to take on new challenges and responsibilities. Our promotion pathways are based on merit and are designed to help employees reach their full potential.
## nternal Opportunities for Career Advancement
- Vertical Mobility: Through our structured promotion pathways, employees are given the opportunity to advance to higher-level roles. Performance reviews and development discussions help identify potential candidates for promotion.
- Horizontal Mobility: We support cross-departmental transfers, allowing employees to broaden their experience and diversify their skill set. This initiative encourages collaboration and innovation across different functions within the organization.
- Transversal Mobility: Employees are encouraged to participate in skill development and cross-training programs to gain transferable skills. This allows them to explore new roles within the company, fostering a culture of adaptability and versatility.
- By fostering internal career mobility, Company ensures that employees have the chance to continuously develop, take on new challenges, and align their career goals with the evolving needs of the organization. This approach supports both individual success and the overall growth of the company, creating a dynamic and engaging work environment for all.
## Leave Entitlements and Policy – Company
## Privilege Leave (PL):
- 1day for every 20 days physically present
- Privilege leave will be calculated and credited in January of every year, on pro rata basis.
- Employee is entitled to privilege leave only if, physical present days is 240 in the calendar year.

chapters.title: Paternity Leave:
chapters.text:
- Management will grant its employees paternity leave off up to 6 working days.
- This leave is applicable for the first born child only.
- this leave can be taken in 2 parts (Maximum) only
## Family Sick Leave
- • Family Sick leave can not be taken for more than 1 day in same month.
- • This leave applicable only in the cases of Family Member’s medical reasons.
- • These leaves cannot be encash.
- • All necessary documents like prescription, doctor certificate, invoices of medicines, tests will have to be submitted to the management. Management retains the right to acknowledge or refuse these certificates. Management also retains the rights to award or adjust extra privilege leaves with the sick leaves.
- • These leaves cannot be carried forward.
- • These leaves cannot be accumulated.
## Leave Without Pay (LWP):
- Eligibility: LWP can be availed when other leave types are unavailable or exhausted. A maximum of 30 days of LWP can be taken with prior approval from the Department Head.
## Shift Change:
- Monthly Shift Schedule: The monthly shift schedule must be assigned through notice board & official whats app group of Jaynix Staff
- Emergency Shift Changes: No shift has been changed/assigned without an approval by HR department
## Weekly Off Change:
- Weekly Off Assignment: Weekly off days will be assigned through ESSL & Keka only which was fixed on each Sunday until & Unless any working sunday.
- Intervening Weekly Off & LWP: Any weekly off or paid holiday falling within a period of absenteeism or LWP will be treated as an absence.

chapters.title: Bonus:
chapters.text:
- Eligibility: Employees who have worked a minimum of 30 working days during the year are eligible for a bonus. The bonus year is from 1st April to 31st March.
- Bonus Calculation: Bonus has been calculated as per the Bonus act regulations & control & monitored by HR & Finance department only.
- Payment of Bonus: Bonus will be paid within 8 months from the end of the accounting year. Employees who leave the organization during the year will receive their bonus as part of the full and final settlement.
## Holidays for the Year 2024:
- Holiday calendar is displayed in “Keka” Portal.
- Also the same has been individually displayed in Notice board to every employee for more information.
Note:
- If a public holiday falls on a weekly off day, no compensatory off (C-off) will be granted.
- The holiday calendar is subject to changes depending on auspicious dates during the year.
## Attendance Recording and Working Hours Policy - Company
- All employees must record their daily attendance to ensure accurate payroll processing. Employees are required to clock in and out at designated locations using the Attendance Recording System (ESSL), which may include Face Recognition or Touch Screen Machines, available at the Company's Factory, Offices, and other locations. This policy aims to streamline the attendance recording process while fostering a culture of trust, integrity, and self-discipline.
- Employees are expected to clock in and clock out at their scheduled shift times using the ESSL machines at the provided locations.
- As part of maintaining discipline and punctuality, employees should ensure they are present at work well before their shifts begin. All Heads of Department (HOD) are required to maintain a minimum of 8.30 hours of presence throughout the day,
- To accommodate unavoidable situations (e.g., vehicle breakdown, traffic jams, personal matters), employees are allowed up to 10 minutes of lateness. Any further delays will be considered late and will result in a leave deduction (from EL/LWP). Employees are expected to inform their managers of delays promptly. Any lateness beyond two occasions will lead to a salary deduction for the late hours or require the employee to apply for a half-day leave. This option is not a quota and should be used only in case of emergencies.
- A minimum of 4 hours of attendance is required on any given day to be counted as a half-day. If attendance is less than 4.5 hours, it will be considered a full day of absence/Leave, subject to the grace period rule. Any lateness or early departure of more than 2 hours will result in being marked absent for a half-day.
- If an employee leaves the office or factory for official or personal work during working hours, they must apply for a Gate Pass singed by immediate supervisor & HR Department. The employee must also Punch out their attendance mark through the ESSL system when leaving.
- If an employee is out for official work and is unable to return before office hours end, they are not required to return just to mark attendance. They can regularize their attendance through “Keka” Portal following approval received by his/her HOD.
- For employees traveling for domestic, international, or off-site work, they can apply “Work On Duty” from “Keka” Portal.
- Employees are expected to plan and apply for leave in advance to ensure attendance is regularized before they proceed on leave.
- In case of emergency or exigency where leave applications cannot be submitted before taking leave, the HR Department will accept the leave application up to a maximum of three working days after the employee returns to work. Any leave application submitted beyond this period will be marked as absent without pay.
## Transparent remuneration Process
At Company, we are committed to ensuring transparency in our remuneration process, ensuring all employees are aware of their salary, benefits, and any additional compensation they may receive. The following outlines how remuneration is determined, communicated, and processed.

chapters.title: Health and Wellness Benefits & Insurance Policy
chapters.text:
Company offers a comprehensive health and wellness program designed to support the physical and mental well-being of its employees, with a strong emphasis on preventive care, emergency support, and overall work-life balance. The following outlines the key benefits provided and the associated insurance coverage details:
## Health and Wellness Benefits:
- Comprehensive Medical Insurance: Company provides medical insurance with coverage up to ₹2,00,000 to ₹5,00,000 annually depends on seniority & tenure, covering hospitalization, surgeries, and treatment for both employee and spouse, and up to two childrens.
- Cashless Treatment Network: Employees can access cashless treatment hospitals across the country as Described in policy details, ensuring smooth and efficient access to care during emergencies.
- Mental Health Support: Company values mental well-being and offers confidential counseling services through certified professionals. Employees are eligible for free therapy sessions and access stress management workshops.
## Health and Accident Insurance Coverage:
Comprehensive health and accident insurance coverage is provided for eligible employees, addressing medical expenses, hospitalization, and accidents occurring during work or while commuting.
This policy applies to all full-time employees working in the office premises of Company, who are not covered under the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948.
Eligibility:
Coverage Details:
- As per the Described under the policy
## Worksman Compensation Policy:
- Coverage includes accidental death, permanent or partial disability resulting from workplace accidents or commuting, and related medical expenses and covers loss of pay during hospitalisation due to accident.
## Exclusions:
- As Described under each individual policy
## Payment Basis:
- Claims can be processed via cashless or reimbursement methods (Excluding Worksman Compensation Policy).
## Costs Exceeding Provided Coverage:
- Employees will have to cover the costs for expenses exceeds the provided limits as Described under the policy.
## Renewal:
- The policy can be renewed annually.
- Employee are added in policy after three months of joining with company.
## Claims Procedure:
- Cashless claims are available at designated hospitals.
- Reimbursement claims must be submitted within 30 days of treatment.
## Claim Settlement:
- Claims settlements are aided by Company’s HR department.
## Employee Provident Fund (EPF) & Employee Pension Scheme (EPS)
## Employee Contribution:
- All employees ( Company or Contractor) are required to contribute 12% of their basic salary (including Dearness Allowance, if applicable) towards the Employee Provident Fund (EPF).
- The contribution will be deducted from the employee's monthly salary by the company.
## Company Contribution:
- The company will contribute an amount equal to the employee’s contribution, which is 12% of their basic salary.
- Of this contribution, 3.67% will be allocated to the Employee Provident Fund (EPF), and 8.33% will be directed towards the Employee Pension Scheme (EPS).
## Nomination:
- Employees are required to complete and submit Form 2 (Nomination and Declaration form), which will designate the beneficiary(ies) to receive the funds in the event of the employee’s death.
- The nominee(s) must be a family member. Any nomination made for someone outside of the family will be considered invalid.
## Pension Payment under Employee Pension Scheme:
- To be eligible for pension benefits, an employee must have completed at least 10 years of contribution towards the P.F Scheme.
- The pension is payable under the following conditions:
- Superannuation (retirement) or Resignation.
- Permanent total disablement or Death during service (in the event of death, the pension will be paid to the nominated beneficiary).
## Anti-Discrimination and Harassment
At Company, we are dedicated to fostering a respectful, inclusive, and fair work environment for all employees. Our commitment to eliminating discrimination and harassment is fundamental to our company’s values, ensuring that every employee has an equal opportunity to thrive. This section outlines our efforts to prevent discrimination and harassment and provides clear guidelines on how we handle such issues.

chapters.title: Anti-Discrimination Policy
chapters.text:
- Equal Opportunity Employment: Company is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to ensuring that all employment decisions—such as hiring, promotions, compensation, and training—are based on merit, qualifications, and job performance without regard to race, color, national origin, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion, or any other characteristic protected by law.
- Prohibited Conduct: Discrimination in any form is prohibited. We do not tolerate unfair treatment or biased decisions based on any protected characteristics. Discrimination may take many forms, such as biased hiring practices, unequal pay, exclusion from career development opportunities, or any behaviour that adversely affects an employee’s performance or well-being.
- Aide for disabled employees: Employees with disability are given appropriate nature of work considering their disability. Necessary workplace instructions are depicted in a form that is understandable for them.
- Policy Enforcement: We take all allegations of discrimination seriously. Each claim will be investigated thoroughly, and any employee found to have engaged in discriminatory behavior will face disciplinary action. Consequences may include counseling, warnings, suspension, or termination, depending on the severity of the conduct.
## Examples of Discrimination:
- Unequal Pay: A qualified employee receiving less pay than their colleagues performing the same job based on gender or ethnicity.
- Unequal Opportunities: A qualified employee being overlooked for a promotion based on their age or disability, despite their strong qualifications and performance.

chapters.title: Anti-Harassment Policy
chapters.text:
- Definition of Harassment: Harassment refers to any behavior, whether physical, verbal, or non-verbal, that creates a hostile, intimidating, or offensive work environment. This includes actions that demean, belittle, or otherwise harm an individual based on their protected characteristics, making it difficult for them to perform their job effectively.
## Types of Harassment:
- Sexual Harassment: Unwelcome sexual advances, inappropriate comments, physical gestures, or requests for sexual favors. This type of harassment creates an uncomfortable and unsafe environment for the individual being targeted. E.g Sending inappropriate or unsolicited messages to a colleague, creating a hostile work environment.
- Bullying: Repeated, unreasonable actions intended to undermine or intimidate an individual. This can include verbal abuse, spreading false rumors, or deliberately sabotaging someone's work or reputation. E.g Making derogatory comments about a colleague’s race or gender, undermining their performance and confidence.
- Retaliation: Any adverse action taken against an employee who has reported harassment or participated in an investigation. Retaliation may include unjustified disciplinary actions, exclusion from team activities, or denial of career advancement opportunities. E.g Taking disciplinary actions or sidelining an employee who reported harassment, deterring others from coming forward.
## Support of Victims:
- We offer support to employees who have experienced harassment, including counseling services and the option to adjust work arrangements if necessary. Ensuring that victims feel protected and supported is a key part of our commitment to maintaining a respectful work environment. Regular training sessions are conducted for all employees, focusing on our anti-discrimination and anti-harassment policies. The training educates employees on how to recognize harassment, the importance of reporting concerns, and how to foster a positive and inclusive workplace.
## Responsibilities and Compliance
- Employee Responsibilities: Every employee is expected to treat their colleagues with respect and fairness. Employees should report any observed or experienced discrimination or harassment to ensure it is addressed promptly and appropriately.
- Manager Responsibilities: Managers and supervisors play a critical role in maintaining a respectful work environment. They are responsible for ensuring their teams are aware of our anti-discrimination and anti-harassment policies, addressing any complaints, and taking proactive steps to prevent incidents. Managers must create a culture where employees feel comfortable voicing concerns without fear of reprisal.
- Monitoring and Review: We continuously review and update our anti-discrimination and anti-harassment practices to reflect any legal changes and the feedback from employees. This ongoing review ensures that our measures remain effective and relevant.
- Consequences for Violations: Any violation of our anti-discrimination or anti-harassment policies will lead to disciplinary action. Consequences may include counselling, reprimands, suspension, or termination, depending on the severity and nature of the offense. We are committed to upholding these standards to protect our employees.
## Preventive Measures
- Clear Communication of Policy: At Company , all employees are provided with a copy of the Harassment Prevention Policy during onboarding and through regular training sessions. This ensures that everyone is well-informed about unacceptable behaviors and understands the potential consequences of such actions.
- Regular Risk Assessments: We conduct regular assessments to identify and evaluate any potential harassment risks within the workplace. This proactive approach helps us address vulnerabilities before they become significant issues.
- Anonymous Reporting Channels: To promote a safe reporting environment, we offer confidential and anonymous reporting options. This encourages employees to report any incidents of harassment without fear of retaliation.
- Active Monitoring: We hold regular feedback sessions to evaluate our workplace culture and address any emerging concerns promptly.
- Support Systems: We have counselling services, to assist employees who may need help in dealing with harassment or other workplace issues.
## Reporting Procedure
Company takes all allegations of discrimination and harassment seriously. To ensure the reporting process is accessible and straightforward, we provide multiple channels for employees to raise concerns:
- Direct Reporting: Employees can report any incidents of discrimination or harassment directly to their immediate supervisor or manager. If you prefer, you can escalate the issue to the Human Resources department.

chapters.title: Training
chapters.text:
## The aim of this training program is to ensure that employees at Company receive appropriate training to enhance their performance, specifically in Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) and their respective roles. The program ensures proper documentation of all training sessions and provides a structured procedure for identifying, planning, executing, and tracking employee training in the manufacturing and support functions.
- This training approach applies to both new and existing employees, including permanent and contract staff.
## Roles and Responsibilities:
## Training Coordinator:
- Oversees the training process for new hires and ensures that on-the-job training is completed before employees start their routine tasks.
- Manages and schedules periodic cGMP training for all employees.
- Develops training plans for cGMP and functional training across various departments.
- Identifies and qualifies trainers within the company, ensuring that the training pool is adequately staffed.
- Coordinates the creation of training materials and facilitates training sessions.
- Tracks employee training progress and escalates issues when necessary.
## Department Training Coordinators:
- Responsible for identifying specific training needs related to departmental Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
- Monitors the progress of employees' training, ensuring timely completion, and reports any delays to the Training Coordinator.
## nstructors/Subject Matter Experts (SMEs):
- Conduct training sessions and share their expertise on relevant topics.
- Serve as primary trainers and facilitate knowledge transfer.
## Human Resources:
- Coordinates the induction training programs for new employees, both onsite and offsite.
- Ensures that all new hires complete the necessary induction and onboarding processes.
## Employees:
- Are responsible for completing all assigned training within the specified timelines.
- Participate actively in training sessions and engage with learning materials.
## Training Procedures:
- Training: Skill Matrix & competency chart will prepared for each employee based on their current competencies.
- Training Needs Identification (TNI): This process helps to identify the training requirements for each role. Training needs are documented and assigned to employees based on their job functions and personal development goals, ensuring that they are equipped to perform their tasks efficiently.
- Training Management System: After identifying training Needs training coordinator will prepare a yearly training Callander scheduled for training sessions to be held through out the year
- Training Calander can be reviewed and revised based on any specific mid year requirements.
## Training for New Permanent Employees:
- Induction Training: All new employees will undergo an initial induction program when joining Company . This training introduces employees to the organization, its policies, and its core functions, as well as health, safety, and environmental protocols. A site-specific induction manual may be prepared for each department to tailor the training content.
- cGMP Training: All employees in roles related to manufacturing, quality control, warehousing, engineering, and quality assurance will receive basic cGMP training. This will cover the essential regulations and expectations surrounding good manufacturing practices, ensuring employees understand the quality standards required in their work.
- Job-Specific Training: New hires will be trained on procedures that are specific to their roles. This training will include SOPs that pertain to their job responsibilities. On-the-job training will be documented and tracked to ensure all necessary training is completed before employees begin their regular tasks.
## Repetitive Strain Prevention and Support
- Workstations: Company provides employees with ergonomic chairs, and computer equipment designed to reduce strain and promote comfortable, healthy posture throughout the workday.
- Regular Movement Breaks: Employees are encouraged to take short, frequent breaks from repetitive tasks to stretch and move, minimizing the risk of strain and fatigue caused by prolonged sitting or repetitive motions.
- Posture and Stretching Education: Regular workshops and training sessions are held to educate employees on proper posture, stretches, and exercises that can help prevent repetitive strain injuries (RSIs) and maintain physical well-being.
- RSI training sessions: Company runs internal training to raise awareness of the risks of repetitive strain injuries and encourage employees to adopt practices that promote joint and muscle health.
- Regular Risk Assessments: Company conducts regular risk assessments to identify tasks or processes that could lead to repetitive strain injuries, ensuring early detection and the implementation of preventive measures to mitigate risks.

chapters.title: Grievance Resolution Procedure
chapters.text:
## Purpose
- The purpose of establishing this grievance resolution procedure is to provide employees with a formal and structured process to raise concerns related to their job, manager, or the work environment. These concerns can range from perceived unfair treatment to issues related to safety or discrimination. By offering a clear and transparent grievance process, Company ensures that employees have a safe space to voice their issues, and these concerns are properly addressed. This procedure aims to identify and resolve workplace issues, thereby fostering a positive and productive work environment.
## Key Benefits
- Fairness and Accessibility: Ensures all employees have equal access to report concerns.
- Transparency: Promotes openness in addressing and resolving grievances.
- Problem Identification: Helps uncover underlying issues that may not be immediately visible.
- Risk Mitigation & Compliance: Reduces potential legal or financial risks associated with unresolved grievances.
- Better Decision-Making: Informed decisions based on facts, improving company policies and practices.
- Improved Workplace: Contributes to a more harmonious and productive environment.
- Enhanced Employee Engagement: Promotes a culture of trust and respect, increasing employee satisfaction.
- Strengthened Organizational Culture: Reinforces company values of fairness, inclusivity, and respect.
- Legal Protection and Reduced Liability: Provides legal safeguards by addressing concerns systematically and reducing the risk of legal disputes.
This includes all employees, regardless of their position, as well as contractors, suppliers, and community members impacted by the company’s operations.
## Definitions
- Grievance: A grievance refers to any work-related issue raised by an employee, perceived as unfair treatment, violation of rights, or any other workplace concern that is detrimental to their well-being, such as unsafe working conditions, unequal pay, harassment, or discrimination.
- Grievance Mechanism: This is the formal, structured process that Company has put in place to ensure that grievances are addressed in a timely, fair, and confidential manner. The grievance mechanism ensures that employees’ concerns are heard and acted upon appropriately.
## Types of Grievances:
Employee grievances may vary but generally fall into the following categories:
- Pay and Benefits: Issues related to salary discrepancies, bonuses, benefits, or payroll errors.
- Working Conditions: Concerns about unsafe, unhealthy, or unpleasant work environments, or unfair scheduling practices.
- Treatment: Issues such as harassment, discrimination, bullying, or lack of recognition from management.
- Workload: Feelings of being insufficient resources, or inadequate support to meet job expectations.
- Communication: Concerns about unclear communication, lack of feedback, or the perception that management is not listening to employees.
Other specific grievances that may arise include:

- Human Resources Department: The HR team is responsible for managing grievances. Employees are encouraged to report their issues using one of the following methods:
- Direct Reporting to HR Manager: Employees can directly approach HR or contact the HR Manager by email at XX@XXXXX.COM
- Department Head: In cases where it is deemed appropriate, employees can report grievances to their immediate department head.
- Grievance Reporting Form: To provide anonymity, employees can submit written grievances using designated reporting boxes placed throughout the company premises.
- Record Keeping: For transparency and to ensure a fair resolution process, all grievances and their resolutions will be documented systematically. This includes:
- Record Keeping: All incidents & Investigation on grievances has been recorded with HR Department for future references.
## Key Documents to Retain:
- The initial grievance form or complaint.
- Correspondence, meeting notes, and emails.
- Investigation materials such as witness statements and evidence. (if applicable)
- Records of any actions or decisions taken during the grievance process.
## Procedure
- Reporting: Grievances must be reported in writing. Employees should submit the complaint via email or letter, detailing the nature of the grievance, the specific issue(s), dates, and any relevant evidence or witnesses.

chapters.title: Whistleblower Procedure
chapters.text:
Jaynix’s Code of Business Conduct and Ethics requires every director, officer, and employee of Jaynix to report any violation of the Code which is known to or reasonably suspected by that individual. Directors, officers, and employees must also report any other known or reasonably suspected improper conduct or incident in relation to Jaynix, including any questionable accounting, internal accounting controls or auditing matters or potential violations of the law. Any matter that should be reported is referred to as an “Improper Activity”.
“Vigilance Officer” is a person, nominated/appointed to receive protected disclosures from complainant, maintaining records thereof, placing the same before the director nominated to play the role of Audit Committee for its disposal and informing the complainant the result thereof.
## Reporting Procedures
1.Employees should immediately report Improper Activity:
(a) To their immediate supervisor, or
(b) To their immediate supervisor’s manager, or
(c) To the Chief Financial Officer of Jaynix, including in a situation where an employee is not satisfied with the actions taken by his or her supervisor or supervisor’s manager. Employees can also choose instead or additionally to report Improper Activity to the Chair of the Board or the Vigilance Officer of Jaynix. or directly mail to the VIgilance officer
2. Officers should immediately report Improper Activity:
(a) To the Chief Financial Officer of Jaynix, or
(b) To the Chair of the Board or the Vigilance Officer of Jaynix.
3. Directors should immediately report Improper Activity to the Chair of the Board or the Lead Director of Jaynix.
4.The contact information for the Chief Financial Officer, the Chair of the Board and the Lead Director is as follows:
(a) Contact by email. Communications may be sent to the following email addresses, which are confidential to the respective individual addressees:
Chief Financial Officer - Kaushik.Lodaya@Jaynix.com
Chair of the Board- Nikhil@Jaynix.com
Vigilance Officer- Uma@Jaynix.com
(b) Contact by mail or other physical delivery. Communications may be mailed or delivered, addressed to the intended recipient:
C/o Jaynix Engineering Private Limited, 171, Horizon Industrial Park, Off NH 48, Bamangam - Por, Vadodara 391 210
Any such communication will be delivered by Jaynix, unopened, to the intended recipient. Directors, officers, and employees may also make reports regarding Improper Activity on a confidential and anonymous basis to the Board of Jaynix.
## nvestigations
1. All reports will be taken seriously. Jaynix will ensure that suitable guidance is available to anyone that receives a report and that appropriate procedures are in place for investigating and tracking reports. Jaynix will ensure that every report will be promptly and thoroughly investigated. The actions taken by Jaynix with respect to a particular report will depend upon the nature of the report. The report may be investigated internally by management, by the Board or an appropriate committee of the Board or be referred to the police and/or the appropriate regulatory authorities. Management will report quarterly to the Board on reports received and the status of outstanding investigations.
2. All information reported and disclosed during an investigation will remain confidential and made available only on a need-to-know basis, except as necessary to conduct the investigation and to take any remedial action, and subject to any applicable law (that can compel disclosure in some circumstances). All directors, officers and employees have a duty to cooperate in the investigation of reports of Improper Activity.
3. If, at the conclusion of its investigation, Jaynix determines that Improper Activity has occurred, Jaynix will take effective remedial action equal to the severity of the offence. This action may include disciplinary action against the accused party up to and including termination and reporting to police and/or regulatory authorities.
4. Jaynix acknowledges that those who file reports need to be assured that their report has been properly addressed. Accordingly, subject to any legal constraints, Jaynix will provide the complainant with appropriate information about the outcome of any investigation within a reasonable period (except in cases where the report was filed anonymously).
## Retention
1. All documents related to the reporting, investigation, and enforcement of this Policy will be kept in accordance with Jaynix’s applicable policies and applicable law.
## No Retaliation
1.This Policy is intended to encourage and enable directors, officers, and employees of Jaynix to raise serious good faith concerns without fear of adverse consequences to them by virtue of raising those concerns. Accordingly, Jaynix will not carry out or, to the fullest extent reasonably within its power, permit any retribution or retaliation of any kind against any individual for submitting any report in good faith.
